answer: A sybil swarm only pays if each extra identity is cheap, so the economy prices identity itself. Every agent posts a bond before earning, and it grows along a referral vine: the more accounts one sponsor introduces, the steeper the stake each newcomer must lock, while payouts to linked identities stay delayed and split. A fake cluster becomes a trellis of costly, slow-to-drain stakes, not free clones. Honest agents reclaim their bond on schedule; a farming cartel must front more capital than it can claim, and detection freezes it like a glacier. Cost per alias is a sunk stake, not a click.
